title: A linkage between flowering phenology and fruit-set success of alpine plant communities with reference to the seasonality and pollination effectiveness of bees and flies
screening_reason: Published study directly pairs estimated bumble-bee or dipteran visitation frequency at the flowering peak with natural fruit-set success and fits year-specific logistic relationships, but the visitation-to-fruit-set logistic coefficients and their sampling uncertainty are not printed and no raw population-level table has yet been recovered.
notes: Mizunaga & Kudo 2017. HUSCAP accepted manuscript is open. Bee- and fly-pollinated lanes are analyzed separately. Table 2 and Table 4 permit reconstruction of seasonal predicted curves, but not a defensible sampling variance for the direct pollinator-frequency -> fruit-set relationship without covariance/raw data.

title: Flowering time and pollinator abundance determine the female reproductive success in the dioecious palm Chamaedorea pinnatifrons (Arecaceae)
screening_reason: Published study measures final fruit set for early/peak/late female inflorescences and independently measures weekly abundance of the specialist thrips pollinator across the same reproductive season. The seasonal partner window can prospectively order low- versus high-availability flowering states, but repeated inflorescences from the same female plants make the published group means and SEs insufficient for an independence-safe strict effect without raw plant identifiers or a source model linking pollinator availability directly to final reproduction.
notes: Cascante-Marín et al. 2025. Fruit set early=0.030±0.009 SE (n=34 inflorescences), peak=0.079±0.013 (n=39), late=0.296±0.027 (n=42). Brooksithrips chamaedorea abundance increased about 13-fold from early March to late May. Do not treat calendar date alone as synchrony or use an independence-assuming early-vs-late variance until plant-level dependence is resolved.

title: Relationships among Flowering Phenology, Insect Visitors, and Seed‐Set of Individuals: Experimental Studies on Four Co‐occurring Species of Goldenrod (Solidago: Compositae)
screening_reason: Published S. graminifolia 1980 data provide independently observed seasonal Apis availability, source-defined early/late clone groups, natural filled-seed means with 95% CIs, and clone sample sizes sufficient for a frozen angular-scale Hedges-g reconstruction.
notes: Strict-H1 source-native SMD closed: Hedges g=+1.140160763709139, variance=0.14974957430600422, n=37, dependence_id DEP_IWE084_SOLIDAGO_APIS. Other Solidago species are excluded from the primary row under source-specific identification rules; no Fisher-z conversion is used.

title: The effect of density-dependent insect visits, flowering phenology, and plant size on seed set of the endangered vernal pool plant Pogogyne abramsii (Lamiaceae) in natural compared to created vernal pools
screening_reason: Published study jointly measured pollinator activity, flowering phenology and seed set, but current public routes do not expose the pool/date and plant-level values needed to pair partner availability with final reproduction at defensible grain.
notes: Schiller et al. 2000. ResearchGate and publisher/DOI retrieval routes were audited and did not yield a usable full-text/data source in the execution environment.

title: Reproduction in Polemonium: Competition for Pollinators
screening_reason: Published source partitions the flowering season by bee:flower availability and reports corresponding seed-set limitation, but exact temporal service-to-seed-set effect magnitude and uncertainty remain behind inaccessible source routes.
notes: Zimmerman 1980. JSTOR returns challenge HTML and the current Wiley/ESA route is Cloudflare-blocked; do not derive an effect from narrative correlation/significance alone.

title: Pollination Efficiency of Bumblebee Queens and Workers in the Alpine Shrub Rhododendron aureum
screening_reason: Four 2007 plots have matched peak-flowering bumblebee visitation and natural fruit set, but the prospectively frozen deterministic vector-PDF extraction of exact plot means failed because Figure 2 is embedded/raster rather than addressable vector markers.
notes: Kudo et al. 2011; terminal under the current source. Manual/raster point clicking is prohibited by the predeclared extraction rule; reopen only if a new exact numerical source appears.
